content.text:
Yes — killed by `systemd-oomd`, not the kernel OOM killer.

**What happened (Aug 28, 19:02:48–19:02:50):**
1. `session-662.scope` killed — swap was 61.4G/67G, memory 126G/134G (>90% both).
2. `session-560.scope` killed 2s later — 12 processes, on memory-pressure rule (54.4% > 40% for >10s).
3. herdr's current PIDs (262751/262752) started **19:02:57**, 7s after the kill, in a fresh `session-667.scope`.

So the old herdr was in one of those killed scopes and came back seconds later. It's up now, RSS 47MB — herdr itself was collateral, not the cause. It has no systemd unit (`herdr.service` not found), so nothing supervises it; the restart was manual or from a wrapper.

**Cause was box-wide memory exhaustion**, and your aggressive oomd config (`etc/systemd/oomd.conf.d/50-aggressive.conf`, deployed 04:59 today) kills the whole session scope — so one hog takes down every process sharing that login session, herdr included.

Next: `journalctl --since 18:50 --until 19:03 | grep -iE 'swap|pressure'` to find what ate 61G of swap right before the kill.

content.text:
Nothing is leaking. You're just running everything at once. 109G/125G used, breakdown by total RSS:

| RSS | Count | What |
|---|---|---|
| 18.5G | 1 | `llama-server` (k8s pod, model weights resident) |
| 10.0G | **33** | `.claude-wrapped` sessions |
| 8.9G | **14** | `.opencode-wrapp` sessions |
| ~15G | — | k8s stack: longhorn (4.3G/89), containerd-shim, rancher, argocd, vector, vmstorage/vmagent, atticd |
| 5.9G | 332 | 300 `zsh` (2.2G) + 32 `node-MainThread` (2.8G) + 73 `gitstatusd` |
| 2.5G | 33 | `python` + 32 `uv` (1.1G) |

**The actual problem: 47 concurrent agent sessions** eating 19G resident plus most of your 31G swap (top swap users are opencode at 1.1G and 1.0G, `warp-svc` at 1.9G, and six `.claude-wrapped` at ~300M each). 300 zsh shells means those sessions are also leaking shells they never reaped.

llama-server at 18.5G is by design — it's a loaded model, it won't shrink. Combined with the k8s cluster you have ~35G of permanent floor, leaving ~90G for interactive work, and the agents fill it.

**Next (30s):** `ps -eo pid,lstart,rss,cmd -C .claude-wrapped --sort=start_time | head -20` — find the oldest sessions. Tell me which PIDs are dead and I'll kill those exact PIDs (not by pattern).
You're right that my table doesn't reconcile — summing RSS is invalid accounting (shared pages get counted once per process, and it ignores kernel/slab/cache entirely). Let me do it properly.

content.text:
Found the missing memory: **28 GiB is pinned by the GPU and invisible to `free`/`ps`.**

`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/mem_info_gtt_used` = **28,138 MB**. GTT is system RAM mapped for amdgpu — it never shows in `AnonPages`, `Slab`, or any process's RSS. VRAM used is only 178 MB, so whatever's on that GPU is running almost entirely out of system RAM.

Real reconciliation against `MemTotal` 125.1 GiB:

| GiB | Source |
|---|---|
| 59.2 | `AnonPages` — all userspace heaps combined |
| 27.5 | **GPU GTT (amdgpu)** — not in any process RSS |
| 15.5 | `Cached` (file cache, 1.4 GiB of it dirty) |
| 6.2 | `Slab` (3.6 reclaimable / 2.5 not) |
| 4.7 | zswap compressed pool — holding 16 GiB of swapped-out anon |
| 2.1 | pagetables 0.5 + kernel stack 0.24 + vmalloc 1.24 + percpu |
| 0.86 | `MemFree` |
| ~9 | unattributed — btrfs metadata, DMA buffers, driver allocs |

Cgroup view, which doesn't double-count: kubepods 49.8G, user.slice 21.9G, docker 8.9G, system.slice 2.2G = 82.8 GiB of cgroup-attributed memory. The GTT and most kernel memory sit outside all of it.

Two corrections to what I said last turn: summing RSS was the wrong method (shared pages counted per-process, kernel memory ignored), and my PSS attempt returned garbage — `smaps_rollup` is unreadable for root-owned processes without sudo, so that command's output was shifted PIDs, not memory. Discard it.

Also: no ZFS, no hugetlb reserved, so neither of the usual "missing RAM" suspects applies.

**What's 195?** I don't have a number matching that anywhere — `MemTotal` is 125 GiB, swap 62.5 GiB (187.6 combined). Tell me where you're seeing 195 and I'll reconcile against it specifically.
